current_leader.name: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention engine
current_leader.state_transition: approved authorization -> capture/reversal absent as scheme deadline approaches -> combine PSP lifecycle state with merchant order/fulfillment state -> recommend CAPTURE/REVERSE/NO ACTION before integrity-fee trigger -> reconcile avoided fee
current_leader.why_survived: Fresh 2026 fee schedules confirm materially sized deterministic penalties: Mastercard processing-integrity fees reach 0.452% with a $0.113 minimum in Moneris' published 2026 schedule, Visa US misuse-of-authorization is $0.15 per non-compliant transaction, and Mastercard introduced a separate 0.0339% authorization-validity fee for final transactions cleared 72-168 hours after authorization. The corrective state is machine-readable and can remain recommendation-only. However Tagada now provides cross-processor authorization-expiry monitoring and automatic capture/re-authorization, reducing competitive whitespace from 4 to 3.
strongest_evidence: Moneris 2026: Mastercard Processing Integrity Final Auth and Not Reversed/Cleared Preauthorization fee 0.452% with $0.113 minimum.
Moneris/TD 2026: Mastercard Authorization Validity Fee 0.0339% on final transactions cleared 72-168 hours after authorization; daily batch close can avoid it.
Visa US misuse-of-authorization fee increased to $0.15 per non-compliant transaction in 2025.

Tagada tracks expiry windows across processors and can alert/auto-capture/re-authorize, demonstrating strong adjacent competition but not an explicit fulfillment-aware stale-authorization reversal-before-integrity-fee product.
current_leader.closest_threat: Tagada payment orchestration is now the strongest adjacent threat because it centrally tracks cross-processor authorization windows and can auto-capture or re-authorize. Shopify also warns before authorization expiry and supports capture-at-fulfillment. Broad scheme-fee intelligence products such as CardTraq, SchemeSense and Recivr cover fee visibility/optimization mainly for issuers/acquirers/processors. No exact merchant-side cross-PSP fulfillment-aware reversal sentinel was found.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read authorization/capture/reversal webhooks and order/fulfillment state; maintain network/MCC/region deadline rules; output REVERSE NOW, CAPTURE NOW, or NO ACTION plus projected avoidable fee. Keep execution merchant-confirmed.
current_leader.monetization: Per prevented-fee event, capped share of reconciled integrity fees avoided, or low monitoring fee only for merchants whose measured exposure exceeds the fee.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Incidence remains unquantified. At Visa's $0.15 misuse fee, low stale-auth rates may not support a product; Mastercard percentage penalties improve economics but may affect a limited subset. Tagada-like orchestration may absorb the control for sophisticated merchants.
current_leader.next_research_test: Obtain merchant/acquirer evidence of processing-integrity fee incidence and dollars per 100k authorizations, segmented by delayed-capture vertical. Search specifically for products that automatically reverse cancelled/unfulfillable authorizations before scheme integrity deadlines. If incidence is low or Tagada/orchestration products already perform this exact reversal decision, demote or reject.

serious_new_candidate.name: Merchant card-network behavior-fee sentinel
serious_new_candidate.state_transition: authorization/decline/capture behavior accumulates toward Visa/Mastercard behavioral-fee threshold -> predict fee before threshold -> recommend configuration/remediation action -> reconcile avoided fee
serious_new_candidate.why_survived: Adyen documents Visa Data Quality fees and Mastercard excessive-authorization fees with explicit machine-readable thresholds; Moneris documents Merchant Advice Code and processing-integrity fee increases. This broadens the money pool beyond stale authorizations while staying potentially read-only.
serious_new_candidate.fatal_or_unresolved_risk: Several remedies require changing retry/risk behavior in the transaction path, and scheme-fee optimization is already served broadly by CardTraq, SchemeSense, PayIP, Recivr and processor-native controls. Therefore it remains below the narrow leader.

fresh_family_findings.reason: Exact first-party/booking software already stores cards and automatically charges no-show fees when status changes, e.g. Resos and SchedulingKit.
Exact real-time meter/battery/control products already forecast peaks and automatically dispatch/load-shift, e.g. Torus and VolTwin.
Fee is real and recurring (UKG lists $55 per off-cycle payroll), but economics are modest and legal/pay-date constraints reduce the decision space.
Per-payout fees and instant-vs-standard spreads are real, but the optimization is usually an obvious cash-timing choice and easy self-serve arithmetic.

new_search_rules: For network behavioral-fee wedges, measure incidence separately from fee rate; a high deterministic penalty does not prove a large recoverable pool.
Treat cross-processor orchestration that already monitors the same state transition as a serious Gate-8 threat even when it markets revenue capture rather than fee prevention.
Prefer the narrow corrective action that does not require sitting in the transaction path; if prevention requires blocking/retrying live payments, penalize Gate 7 and permission scores.
Behavioral scheme fees may form a larger adjacent family, but do not broaden the leader unless the umbrella remains monetizable and less crowded than the narrow wedge.
